1. The benches measure gas per function, fresh and cached, for every bench group in benches/src/main.rs. Keep every group and every measured call, so the report keeps the same rows.
2. Replace the e2e framework with devnet helpers. Deployments use devnet::deploy with the WASM from a directory, not from the workspace target, so add an override: read the environment variable BENCH_WASM_DIR when it is set (the directory that holds the <name>.wasm files), and default to the workspace target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release directory otherwise. We will run the same benches on v0.3.0 WASMs and on the new WASMs against the same devnet, so the harness must not care which build it gets. Put that logic in the benches crate (not in lib/devnet, which you do not own).
3. Gas numbers come from the receipts (L2 gas used, as the old report does; keep get_l2_gas_used and the report format).
4. Keep the optimisation options (Opt::None, Opt::Cache, Opt::CacheWasmOpt): they choose which WASM file is deployed and whether the contract is cached on chain. Cache with `cargo stylus cache bid` is not available from the devnet helper; implement caching through the ArbWasmCache precompile with alloy (the sol! binding for ArbWasmCache.cacheProgram, which the SDK's stylus-tools also uses), or document in the report which options you could not reproduce.
5. The old `scripts/bench.sh` runs `cargo run -p benches`. Keep that working.
6. Do not run the benches yourself on the shared devnet while other agents run E2E tests: the lockf convention applies to benches too. Use `RPC_URL=http://localhost:55000 lockf /tmp/bench/e2e.lock cargo run -p benches` when you need a run, and write the output to /tmp/bench/logs/e5-bench.log.

Requirements for templates/crypto-erc20: it is a template crate. Its tests must keep every test name and every assertion, use TestVM, and build for wasm32 and native.

Requirements for examples/basic/token and examples/basic/script: port them like the other examples. Their scripts are plain binaries that deploy and call contracts; keep their behaviour.

Write check logs under /tmp/bench/logs/e5-*.log. Your final message is the report described in the brief (at most 40 lines), including the bench output summary (number of rows, and any group that failed).

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)

Accessors (global -> VM):
  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).

Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)

  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl

  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)

# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)

Accessors (global -> VM):
  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).

Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
Import paths:
  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())

  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.

  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.

Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }

  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.

  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())

      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)

      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.

- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)

name: check-import
# This workflow checks that developers can import the contracts and crypto library.
permissions:
  contents: read
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, v*]
  pull_request:
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
jobs:
  check-import:
    name: Check Import
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@v1
        with:
          rustflags: ""
          cache: true
          target: wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache cargo-stylus binary
        id: cache-cargo-stylus
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cargo/bin/cargo-stylus
          key: cargo-stylus-0.6.3-${{ runner.os }}

      - name: Install cargo-stylus
        if: steps.cache-cargo-stylus.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: cargo install --locked --force cargo-stylus@0.6.3

      - name: Verify cargo-stylus installation
        run: cargo stylus --version

      - name: Replace path dependencies with git dependencies
        working-directory: templates/crypto-erc20
        run: |
          # Get current commit SHA
          COMMIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

          # Replace path dependencies with git references
          sed -i \
            -e "s|path = \"../../lib/crypto\"|git = \"https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/rust-contracts-stylus.git\", rev = \"$COMMIT_SHA\"|g" \
            -e "s|path = \"../../contracts\"|git = \"https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/rust-contracts-stylus.git\", rev = \"$COMMIT_SHA\"|g" \
            Cargo.toml

          # Verify changes
          grep -E "(openzeppelin|git =|rev =)" Cargo.toml | head -10

      - name: Run tests
        working-directory: templates/crypto-erc20
        run: cargo test

      - name: Build and check contract
        working-directory: templates/crypto-erc20
        run: cargo stylus check -e=https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc

      - name: Export ABI
        working-directory: templates/crypto-erc20
        run: cargo stylus export-abi
